- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.9) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.7) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 3–8% to avoid overreacting to pessimism.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for over-optimism.
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction of 1–3% per day to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows alternating extremes (e.g., +1.13, -1.57, +1.13), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting sentiment noise.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast starts above 75 and true outcome drops below 70, apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–4% per day until price stabilizes.
